primary_topics: Chapter 7 of 'Justice and Faith' -- CJP's commencement address at the University of Iloilo on March 21, 1997, accepting the Doctor of Laws honoris causa from Congressman Alberto J. Lopez and addressing graduates 'poor, struggling but full of energy and ready to battle life's challenges'

An autobiographical retelling of the Sampaloc-to-Supreme-Court arc -- public-school childhood, newspaper-and-shoeshine boy, FEU instead of UP because of a 15-centavo bus fare, Salonga's mentorship, top-ten 1960 bar, Yale denied for the same fare reason, Hong Kong wealth lost in the 1982 stock-market crash, Rotary Manila 1983 meeting with PC chief Ramos, seven JBC bypassings 1992-1995

Three concise lessons distilled from the life-story -- (1) adversities are preludes to greater victories; (2) do not lose heart (illustrated by Anthony Robbins's age-list of Lincoln's defeats); (3) have faith in God (Isaiah 55:8-9 and Romans 8:28)
A closing parable (the farmer with a runaway horse -- 'good luck, bad luck, who knows?') and the synthesizing maxim 'work as if everything depended on you, and pray as if everything depended on God'
sub_topics: Acceptance of honorary degree note -- Leni is a professor at the Asian Institute of Management and the five Panganiban children all have at least one postgraduate degree from a leading university abroad, so the honoris causa finally gives CJP a postgraduate credential of his own (joke)

stances.claim: Adversities and misfortunes are often preludes to greater victories -- FEU (not UP) brought Salonga; denied Yale fares produced Baron Travel funding five overseas master's; the Hong Kong crash freed CJP to return home and be appointed to the Supreme Court.
stances.rhetorical_move: reframing-through-retrospect: setbacks are read as preconditions of the victories that followed

stances.claim: The right response to defeat is to keep working -- Lincoln lost again and again from age 31 through 58 (Anthony Robbins's list) and won the US presidency at 60; graduates should believe in their infinite capacity to ride over defeat.
stances.rhetorical_move: exemplary-figure: a tabulated age-list of failures used as catechism

stances.claim: Faith in God means trusting that He answers prayers 'in His own way, not our way, and in His own time, not our time' -- Isaiah 55:8-9 and Romans 8:28 are the operative anchors.
stances.rhetorical_move: scriptural-anchoring: two verses recruited as the third lesson's spine

stances.claim: Only God truly knows what is good luck and what is bad luck -- the farmer's runaway horse, the nine wild horses, the broken leg, the war that spared the disabled son -- and the integrating maxim is 'work as if everything depended on you, and pray as if everything depended on God.'
stances.rhetorical_move: parable-as-synthesis: a single story collapses three lessons into one practice

stances.claim: Material wealth can vanish (Hong Kong 1982) but achievements like a seat on the Supreme Court are 'money cannot buy, nor can any stock market crash take away' -- a hierarchy of goods underwrites the speech's autobiographical arc.
stances.rhetorical_move: value-hierarchy: vocational gifts ranked above commercial fortunes

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 7 of 'Justice and Faith' is CJP's commencement address at the University of Iloilo on March 21, 1997, accepting the LL.D. honoris causa conferred by his long-time friend Congressman Alberto J. Lopez. Rather than 'a pompous lecture,' CJP tells the graduates his story -- Sampaloc poverty, newsboy, bootblack, peddling cigarettes and bibles; Mapa High honors and a UP scholarship he could not take up because his father lacked the 15-centavo bus fare from Cataluña St. to Diliman, so he enrolled at FEU instead 'walking distance from our house'; the youngest FEUCSO presidency and NUSP co-founding where he met Leni Carpio of St. Scholastica's; Salonga's mentorship and the top-ten bar in 1960; an admission to Yale Law that he could not take up for the same fare reason; his Hong Kong wealth years swept away in the 1982 stock-market crash; the 1983 Rotary Manila induction at which he met then-PC chief Gen. Fidel V. Ramos who, twelve years later, appointed him to the Supreme Court after seven JBC bypassings. From this arc CJP distills three lessons. First, adversities are preludes to greater victories -- FEU instead of UP brought Salonga; the denied Yale fare produced Baron Travel and funded five children's overseas master's degrees; the Hong Kong crash freed him to return home and reach the Supreme Court ('an achievement that money cannot buy nor can any stock market crash take away'). Second, do not lose heart -- Anthony Robbins's tabulated age-list of Abraham Lincoln's defeats (31, 32, 34, 35, 36, 43, 46, 48, 55, 56, 58) ends with the US presidency at 60. Third, have faith in God -- Isaiah 55:8-9 ('my thoughts are not your thoughts...my ways are not your ways') and Romans 8:28 ('God makes all things work for the good of those who love Him'). He closes with the four-act farmer's-horse parable ('good luck, bad luck, who knows? Only God knows!') and the synthesizing maxim: 'We will work as if everything depended on us. And we will pray as if everything depended on God.'
